card.name: The word also after a verb
card.fires_on: The word "also" placed right after an auxiliary verb like "is" or "can" in the middle of a clause. It is most common in the MAOI-with-linezolid-or-methylene-blue sentence of antidepressant labels.

modes.label: Label MAOI sentence
modes.description: "also" after "is" in the sentence saying starting the drug in a patient on linezolid or methylene blue is also contraindicated.
modes.example: Starting citalopram in a patient who is being treated with MAOIs such as linezolid or intravenous methylene blue is<< also>> contraindicated because of an increased

modes.label: General prose
modes.description: "also" after a verb or noun in technical or scholarly text, before an adverb or participle.
modes.example: Because we have chosen a conjugate prior, the marginal likelihood can<< also>> be easily computed by evaluating the following equality

card.writes: It boosts adverbs of scope such as primarily, mainly and chiefly, and suppresses "also"-type words.
card.plain: It marks the little word "also" slipped into a sentence after a verb, as in "is also contraindicated".
